blocks.text: LAHAUL, Himachal Pradesh — For six days, Dechen Wangmo walked through some of the most spectacular landscapes of the Indian Himalayas. But beyond the snow-capped peaks, rivers and mountain villages, she witnessed something deeply troubling: a landscape and a way of life undergoing profound changes. Covering more than 100 kilometers and passing through seven villages in the Garsha region of Himachal Pradesh, India, the former Bhutan Broadcasting Service (BBS) journalist encountered communities struggling with the growing impacts of climate change.
